notes: Both coders found the same five documents (four university-layer pages: AI guidelines hub, student guidelines, Academic Standards syllabus page, Stearns Center AI text generators page; one computing-layer page: CS honor code, archived copy dated 2026-01-24) and set the same stance on every document (delegates x4, restrict x1). Main disagreements and how they were resolved: (1) unit_stance, the most frequent split (neutral vs permit/require/restrict): resolved by whether the sentence takes a position on using AI. Verification and responsibility duties, risk warnings, and rationales became neutral. (2) phase: general vs during-work, and course-start vs during-work/when-misuse for sample-syllabus or template wording; resolved as course-start when the text is what a syllabus tells students, during-work when it governs a task, general for principles. (3) actor: student vs instructor vs admin for template rationales and descriptions of faculty practice; resolved by who the sentence addresses (template wording read by students is student; a duty placed on faculty is instructor). (4) policy_type splits: P56 vs P02 and P56 vs P45 (kept P56 for institution-level framing), P29 vs P31 for 'you will be responsible for any incorrect ... information' (P29), P40 vs P47 for instructor disclosure of detector use (P47), P44 vs P35 for activities built around AI text generation (P35), P04 vs P09 for unit support of the syllabus statement (P09), P10 vs P50 for recording consent (P50), and P03 vs UNCOVERED for scholarship-application advice (P03). General-conduct bans on fabricating data or records, and honor-code advice on securing one's own work, were set to UNCOVERED because no type says the same thing; job-application cover letter advice and wording advice ('compose'/'write') are UNCOVERED too. (5) modality: informs vs should/must-not for 'may be a violation' and for pointers to approved tools (informs); 'shall be reviewed' became must. Only-A units (19): 17 kept as real statements (principles preamble, AI literacy duty, Academic Standards Policy prohibition, student bias and recording-privacy statements, detector unreliability, search-engine comparison, faculty-support and redesign suggestions, honor-code examples-not-exhaustive), 2 dropped (two bullets of the honor code's outside-help list that repeat the rule A already coded as the list preamble and do not mention AI). Only-B units (7): all kept (AI Task Force origin sentence, PII advice in the tutoring section, scholarship-rejection consequence, template rationale about prompt engineering, intellectual-property consult advice, wording advice, a second ask-first sentence in the honor code). One A/B pair was split because the anchors sat in different sentences (scholarship discouragement vs rejection consequence), and one student-page sentence was split into two rules (claiming AI output as one's own is a violation; use not explicitly allowed is a violation). Final file has 198 units. new_types empty on both sides. No school-layer policy found; course layer deferred.
